title: Cross Entropy is Asymmetric
full_prompt:
Write a ManimGL script to visualize why cross entropy is asymmetric ($H(P, Q) \neq H(Q, P)$).

Create a custom `EntropyChart` class that inherits from `VGroup`. This chart should represent a probability distribution as a horizontal bar of stacked segments (representing probabilities $p_i$ summing to 1) at the bottom, and vertical bars rising from each segment representing the information content ($-\log_2 p_i$ bits).

The `EntropyChart` should support:
1. Dynamic updates of the distribution using `ValueTracker`s.
2. Redrawing of the vertical bars using `always_redraw` so that their heights dynamically scale with $-\log_2 p_i$ and align perfectly with the horizontal segments.
3. Color interpolation for the bars.

In the main scene `CrossEntropyIsAsymmetric`:
1. Instantiate two different probability distributions, $P$ and $Q$.
2. Display their respective `EntropyChart`s side-by-side or stacked.
3. Show the calculation of the entropy $H(P)$ and $H(Q)$ as the expected value of the bar heights under their own distributions.
4. Demonstrate cross entropy $H(P, Q)$ by taking the bar heights (code lengths) from distribution $Q$ and placing them on top of the probability segments of distribution $P$. Show that the resulting expected length is different from $H(P)$ and also different from $H(Q, P)$ (which is the bar heights of $P$ on the segments of $Q$).
5. Highlight the inequality $H(P, Q) \neq H(Q, P)$ with clear text and visual cues.

common_failure_modes.pattern: Missing custom StackedProbDistribution class or equivalent implementation in standard Manim
common_failure_modes.note: StackedProbDistribution is a custom 3b1b class; if not defined, it must be implemented manually using VGroup and Rectangles.

common_failure_modes.pattern: Incorrect alignment of vertical information bars with horizontal probability segments
common_failure_modes.note: The bars must dynamically align to the top of the corresponding horizontal segments as the distribution changes.
